title: Para que + subjunctive: why the Church did things

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *para que* + subjunctive from B1 Unit 4 (*para que no pierdas la oportunidad*): it gives the purpose of an action when the people involved are different. Texts about the colony often use the present for past events, so the subjunctive after *para que* is in the present too.

sections.title: Different subjects or the same
rows: Los frailes aprenden lenguas para que los indígenas entiendan el mensaje.
Los frailes aprenden lenguas para entender a los indígenas.

items.spanish: El papa da ese derecho a los reyes para que lleven el cristianismo a las nuevas tierras.
items.english: The pope gives that right to the kings so that they bring Christianity to the new lands.

items.spanish: Los frailes aprenden lenguas indígenas para que los indígenas entiendan el mensaje.
items.english: The friars learn indigenous languages so that the indigenous people understand the message.

items.spanish: Se fundan universidades para que los jóvenes estudien en América.
items.english: Universities are founded so that young people study in America.

items.spanish: Los frailes escriben gramáticas para aprender mejor las lenguas.
items.english: The friars write grammars to learn the languages better.

sections.content: Ask who does each verb. If the subject changes, use *para que* and the subjunctive (*entiendan*, *estudien*). If it is the same person, use *para* + infinitive.
